chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Section leader and rehearsal master of the Basie band
summary: A book quotes praise of Royal as section leader; Royal says he did most of the band's leading through rehearsal, and has been a straw boss for decades.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: In a book published in England in 1957 by Raymond ________, there's some interesting material on you and some pictures. The book is Count Basie and there's a quote from Ernie ________ and he says that, 'I think that Marshal Royal is the best ________ leader a band could have. He's a thoroughly ________ and experienced musician and knows his job inside out. We think he gets a little hard at times, but

someone has to to get results. You know how ________ and erratic a bunch of guys can get at times. He's a great section leader and knows how to rehearse a band and shoulders a lot of the responsibility that would become too demanding of Basie. I learned so much under his leadership."
What kind of things did you ________ and do you think you were a little hard at times?

Not really. To actually be a leader of a band or -- I wasn't the true leader of the band -- of I don't know the way that a leader can really be expressed as being the leader. Count Basie was the owner of the band, but actually he wasn't the leader of the band because I did most of the leading of the band. There are certain things that are necessary in composing a band, putting it together and making them play. The most important part of it is the rehearsing of the band.

It's the same thing as with any other activity that calls for teamwork -- athletic, musically or otherwise. It's precision that counts and the Basie band that I helped him to put together was a well-organized, well-rehearsed, precision band, which is my stick. That's the way that I think that things are supposed to be done. If there's any harshness or hardness that goes along with telling a person what you think is right and wanting them to respond, well, then, I was hard. Otherwise, I don't think I was hard. I think I was just being
correct, which is what it's all about.

See, this has been my job in practically every band since I became 18 or 19 years old. I was seemingly always the guy that they used to call the concert master. That was one of my nicknames. They used to call me a whole lot of other things other than that, but my -- (Laughter.) -- one of my nicknames was the Concert Master, which a lot of fellows still call me because I was always seemingly the guy that showed a whole lot of other fellows that hadn't been so fortunate as I to have legitimate education in music on their instruments or whatever it happened to be. I hope I'm not throwing my words together doubly, but I was fortunate by having musical parents and being in a position to gain a liberal education through the high school level that I could be able to help some of my other friends that hadn't had all of their education musically. So, for that reason, by me being a little bit better prepared, practically every job I've ever had with any band that I've ever been, I've been the so-called straw boss, music director or coordinator or whatever it is, right on down to -- until today.
